items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: I’m so glad that Bob Thiele was able to talk him into it

ctx.x: You just gave me a flashback. I was privileged to do a session with James Moody years ago and I happened to have his most recent CD with me, which was a tribute to Henry Mancini. So I told him how much I enjoyed it and he was like, “Yeah, but that’s not what I wanted to do.” James Moody.

Yeah. I’ve heard tell that John Coltrane didn’t necessarily want to make the ballads album, but I’m so glad that Bob Thiele was able to talk him into it because this is our favorite listening record around here.
So as a composer I see a piano behind you. Where do your compositional ideas start?
